Commercial Roofers in Lewisville

Lewisville has grown into one of the more built-up retail and office corridors in this part of Forsyth County, with shopping centers, medical and professional office buildings, and a mix of newer and older construction along Shallowford Road and Lewisville-Clemmons Road. It's suburban retail roofing more than industrial roofing — multi-tenant centers, office parks, and the maintenance schedules that come with keeping tenants operating through a roof's service life. Commercial roofing contractors and local commercial roofers serve businesses in Lewisville with repair, replacement, coatings, maintenance, inspections, and roof reports.

Multi-Tenant Retail Centers and Rooftop Unit Density

Retail centers along Shallowford Road tend to carry more rooftop HVAC units per square foot than a single-tenant building, since each tenant space typically has its own unit rather than sharing central air. That density means more curbs, more penetrations, and more opportunities for a poorly-flashed unit replacement to compromise the field membrane around it. When a tenant swaps out an HVAC unit independent of any roofing work, the curb flashing sometimes gets patched rather than properly re-integrated, and that shows up as a leak months later traced back to a mechanical contractor's work rather than the roofing system itself.

We recommend property managers require sign-off from the roofing warranty holder any time a mechanical contractor touches a rooftop curb, since most manufacturer warranties have language that voids coverage around unauthorized roof penetrations. That single requirement, written into a lease or a vendor policy, catches most of the warranty problems we see on multi-tenant centers before they ever happen.

Office Building Roofs and Tenant Improvement Conflicts

The professional and medical office buildings along this corridor see a similar pattern — tenant improvements add rooftop equipment for server rooms, supplemental cooling, or signage, and those additions accumulate over a building's life without always being tracked against the original roof plan. Before quoting work on one of these buildings we compare current rooftop conditions against whatever roof plan or as-built documentation is available, so the scope reflects what's actually up there rather than what was there when the building was constructed.

Office buildings here also change tenants more often than the warehouse and manufacturing accounts elsewhere in this market, which means rooftop equipment turns over more frequently too. A curb that was properly flashed for one tenant's cooling unit doesn't automatically work for the next tenant's different equipment footprint, and we flag that mismatch during inspection rather than assuming an existing curb is still doing its job correctly.

What Shallowford Road Roof Inspections Typically Show

  • HVAC curb flashing disturbed by mechanical contractors during equipment swaps
  • Membrane wear concentrated around dense clusters of rooftop units on multi-tenant centers
  • Sealant failure at parapet copings facing direct afternoon sun exposure
  • Drain clogging from landscaping debris on buildings with adjacent tree cover
  • Seam issues at older EPDM sections nearing the end of typical service life

The density of rooftop equipment in this corridor means more inspection points per roof than a comparable building in a less-developed part of the network, and we budget inspection time accordingly.

Coordinating Re-Roofs Across Multiple Tenants

A re-roof on a multi-tenant center along Shallowford Road has to account for lease terms and tenant operating hours that a property manager sets, alongside the roofing schedule itself. We work from whatever phasing the property manager needs to keep tenants operational, and we document each phase separately for warranty purposes since different bays sometimes have different remaining roof life and don't need replacement on the same timeline.

Warranty Continuity on Older Buildings

Some of the older office and retail buildings in Lewisville have been re-roofed once or twice already, sometimes by different contractors with different manufacturer systems. Before adding another layer of work, we confirm what's actually under the current membrane and what warranty, if any, is still active, rather than assuming a clean slate. A building with two prior membrane generations underneath needs that history documented before a third layer goes on, since some manufacturer warranties limit how many times a roof can be recovered rather than torn off. Property managers overseeing several buildings across this corridor also tend to standardize on a smaller set of approved membrane systems over time, which simplifies spare-material inventory and speeds up emergency repairs when a leak comes in outside normal business hours.

Questions From Lewisville Property Owners

Does an HVAC unit swap by another contractor affect my roof warranty?

It can, if the curb flashing isn't restored to the original specification. We recommend requiring the roofing warranty holder to inspect and sign off on any mechanical work that disturbs a roof penetration.

Can a multi-tenant center be re-roofed in phases without disrupting all tenants at once?

Yes — we plan phasing around lease terms and tenant operating hours set by the property manager, documenting each phase separately for warranty purposes.

How do you determine the scope on a building that's already been re-roofed once?

We confirm what system is currently in place and whether any warranty is still active before recommending a new scope, rather than assuming the building needs a full tear-off.

Why do office buildings with server rooms need special roof review?

Supplemental cooling units for server rooms are often added after original construction, and the curb and flashing details need review since they weren't part of the original roof plan.

How often should a busy retail corridor roof be inspected?

More frequently than a lower-traffic building given the rooftop equipment density here — we recommend at least an annual inspection with additional checks after any mechanical work.
